subject: reasoning
question:
A, B, C, D, J, K and L are sitting around a circular table, facing the centre of the table. L sits to the immediate right of D. Only three people sit between L and C when counted from the left of L. Only three people sit between D and J. A sits to the immediate right of K.

How many people sit between D and K when counted from the right of K?
solution:
Given: A, B, C, D, J, K and L are sitting around a circular table, facing the center of the table.

1) L sits to the immediate right of D.

2) Only three people sit between L and C when counted from the left of L.

3) Only three people sit between D and J.

4) A sits to the immediate right of K.

So, B will sit on the remaining place.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/9c1652ee9e35d2d3b41a5e47ba828eb87ab06e084956a08ecf1c68acfaca8ffd.png] 

There is one people sitting between D and K if counted from the right.

Hence, the correct answer is "Option 4".
